what_it_does: Running a quantized neural network — one where the weights have been converted from 32-bit floating-point numbers to compact 4-bit or 8-bit integers to save memory and speed up computation — requires doing large numbers of integer multiplications very efficiently. Standard CPU vector units (the parts of a CPU that process many numbers simultaneously, such as ARM's SVE extension or RISC-V's SIMD instructions) were designed for wider, fixed-size data types and cannot efficiently handle the small integer precisions used in quantized AI models. CAMP (Cartesian Accumulative Matrix Pipeline) is a new hardware design for the multiplier circuits inside those vector units that decomposes each small-integer multiplication into a two-level structure inspired by Cartesian products (all pairings of elements from two sets), allowing the same physical hardware to handle both 4-bit and 8-bit integer operations efficiently. The design was built into real chips: an ARM A64FX processor prototype fabricated at TSMC's 7-nanometer process and a RISC-V edge chip at GlobalFoundries' 22-nanometer process, adding only 1% and 4% extra chip area respectively.
